journey.name: TL-13 An undo that fails offers the task again
journey.description:
REGRESSION GUARD. This journey used to assert the defect: `onUndoDelete` cleared the message before the call, so a restore that failed took the offer with it and the task - whose only copy lived inside that message - was gone for good. Filed as issue #13 and now fixed: the offer is consumed on the way in and re-posted if the restore fails.
The 15% failure rate makes this a routine outcome rather than an exotic one - roughly one undo in seven took this path against the shipped defaults - which is what makes it worth pinning on a device rather than leaving to the ViewModel test that covers the same branch as state.
The failure is read first and the offer waits behind it, because a message may not displace a pending `TaskDeleted`. Both snackbars are `SnackbarDuration.Long`, about ten seconds, so the broadcast has to land inside that window. Send it immediately after reading the message.
Preconditions: adb shell am force-stop com.rounds.test.to_dolist adb shell am start -n com.rounds.test.to_dolist/.MainActivity --es qa_failure_rate 0.0

actions.action: Tap the element with the content description "Delete task" on the "Book dentist" row
Verify that a message reading "Task deleted" is on screen
Using adb, break the source with `am broadcast -n com.rounds.test.to_dolist/.qa.QaControlReceiver -a com.rounds.test.to_dolist.QA_SET_FAILURE_RATE --es qa_failure_rate 1.0`
Tap the "Undo" action on that message
Verify that "No connection. Check your network and try again." is on screen
Verify that "Book dentist" is not on screen
Using adb, heal the source with `am broadcast -n com.rounds.test.to_dolist/.qa.QaControlReceiver -a com.rounds.test.to_dolist.QA_SET_FAILURE_RATE --es qa_failure_rate 0.0`
Wait ten seconds for the failure message to expire
Verify that a message reading "Task deleted" with an "Undo" action is on screen again
Tap the "Undo" action on that message
Verify that "Book dentist" is on screen again
Verify that exactly four elements with the content description "Delete task" are on screen
